All tests pass. Here's what changed and why each decision was made:

**`Command.java`** — generic `@FunctionalInterface` with `T execute()`. Generic over `T` rather than fixed `int` so future commands can return `String`, `long`, or any other type without a second interface. `@FunctionalInterface` means any no-arg lambda is a valid `Command` implementation — no boilerplate class needed.

**`GcdCommand`** — now `implements Command<Integer>`. The `execute()` override is `public` (required by the interface) and returns `Integer` (autoboxed). The class still owns the operands; the interface only governs what callers can see.

**`EuclideanAlgorithmApp.main`** — `command` is declared as `Command<Integer>`, not `GcdCommand`. The concrete type is only mentioned once, at construction. Swapping the implementation doesn't touch the rest of `main`.

**`EuclideanAlgorithmTest.assertCommand`** — takes `Command<Integer>`, not `GcdCommand`. The new lambda test case (`() -> EuclideanAlgorithm.gcd(12, 8)`) demonstrates that the interface is genuinely abstract — callers can compose arbitrary `Command<Integer>` implementations without subclassing `GcdCommand`.
